Definition: of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman:--Sergius.
BiblicalUsage: Sergius is Sergius Paulus, the deputy of Cyprus, a prudent man. He called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Sergius matters because a Roman ruler asked to hear the word — and the word came, and the sorcerer was blinded, and the deputy believed.
